Security & Compliance.description:
The Global Infrastructure and Operations (GIO) Security & Compliance Service Line is a transversal organization within Air Liquide dedicated to designing, building, and operating the security solutions that protect the Group. Under the leadership of Director Jean-Charles MARTIN, the service line is structured into several specialized teams to manage the full lifecycle of cybersecurity, from strategy and innovation to operations and incident. The organization is divided into five primary functional teams and three regional management offices to ensure global coverage and local proximity:1
Governance & Service Management (Mehdi GASMI): Responsible for defining service strategy, managing the lifecycle of service offerings, ensuring steering and governance, and managing strategic vendor contracts.1
Engineering & Innovation (Guillaume LARDEUX): Focuses on designing security solutions, providing technical expertise, leading major projects, and conducting technology watches.1
Transition & Operations (Grégoire PENET): Manages platform operations, administration, monitoring, incident management, and the definition of operational standards.
CSIRT (Pierre-Olivier MARTIN): The Computer Security Incident Response Team is dedicated to detecting, analyzing, and delivering responses to cybersecurity incidents.
Cybersecurity Roadmap Coordination (Bassam ZINE): Coordinates the overall Cybersecurity Roadmap and interfaces with the broader Digital & IT (D&IT) governance.
Regional Managers: Located in Europe, Africa, Middle-East & India (Vincent CAO), the Americas (Brian EASTERLING), and Asia (Chiew Geok NG) to manage local projects, demand pipelines, and escalations.
Core Services and Responsibilities
The Security & Compliance service line manages several critical infrastructure and governance services: Identity & Access - 	Managed through CARM (Centralized Access Rights Management) and AdminPass (Privileged Access Management). 
Network Security	 - Operates Secure Web Gateways (SWG) and Firewalls; currently transitioning to SSE (Secure Service Edge) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) for Zero-Trust connectivity. Cloud Security- Transitioning from Prisma Cloud to Cortex Cloud (integrated with Cortex XSIAM) to provide AI-powered security management across multi-cloud environments. Application Protection - WAAP (Web Application & API Protection) provides enhanced security and bot management for critical applications through. Compliance & Hardening - Enforces server security standards (GT04) using tools like Qualys for automated compliance assessment. PKI & Certificates -Manages the Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM) project to automate public and private certificate renewals via Sectigo

Command Center.description:
The Command Center Service Line, formerly referred to as GOPs, is a centralized transversal organization within Air Liquide Global Infrastructure and Operations. It serves as the dedicated hub for monitoring, managing, and coordinating digital operations to ensure the stability, availability, and security of the Group infrastructure.

The service line is led by Director Graeme White and is structured to provide 24/7 global coverage through functional leads and regional managers. The global leadership includes Transition and Operations Lead Reshania Misra, while regional management is handled by Raj Ramamoorthy for the Americas, Jey Muniandi for Asia-Pacific, and Karl Serdar for Europe, Africa, Middle-East, and India. Specialized functional roles include Karim Rahmani as Operations Expert Lead and Sidonie Chantoury for Major Incident Management.

The Command Center is currently undergoing a transformation to move from a reactive posture to a proactive, intelligence-driven orchestration model. Its core services include Major Incident Management for the standardized coordination and resolution of critical global incidents, and Observability and Monitoring to anticipate issues before they impact business operations. The service line also manages Service Orchestration through SIAM, maintains Data and CMDB Quality for accurate operational reporting, and utilizes AIOps and Automation for automated incident response.

User Workplace.description:
The User Workplace Service Line is a transversal organization within Air Liquide’s Global Infrastructure and Operations (GIO) responsible for designing and implementing the digital environment provided to employees. This encompasses hardware such as PCs, mobile devices, and video conferencing, alongside software suites like Google Workspace and enterprise application stores, and on-site or remote support services.

The service line is led by Director Jérôme Bachelerie and is organized into functional teams and regional management to balance global strategy with local proximity. Key leadership roles include:
Governance and Service Management: Guillaume Chirol leads this team, which defines service strategy and manages the service portfolio and strategic vendor contracts.
Engineering and Innovation: François Desideri manages this group, which is responsible for designing workplace solutions and leading major technical projects.
Transition and Operations: Managed by Béatrice Lubrano, this team oversees operational standards and continuous improvement plans.
Business Office: Dieter Heming leads this team, which focuses on asset management and service line activity reports.
Regional Managers: Olivier Pirz leads the Europe, Africa, Middle-East, and India region; Asgar Bhallo manages the Americas; and Revin Imasalam leads Asia.
Current strategic initiatives for 2026 include:
Modern Management Project: This initiative aims to enhance the employee experience for PC and mobile devices by implementing a cloud-based management solution. A pilot for this "Modern Experience" is scheduled for mid-2026 to validate the migration process and device performance.
Zero-Trust Transformation: The service line is replacing traditional VPNs with Zscaler Private Access to modernize remote connectivity. Full decommissioning of the legacy Ivanti solution is targeted for October 2026.
Consistent Print Management: This project will implement a single, centralized Managed Printing Services solution to ensure security compliance across the global printer fleet.
User Experience Improvements: Ongoing efforts include enhancing the MyItCorner self-help portal and expanding chatbot and ServiceNow automation capabilities to reduce support tickets and improve satisfaction.

Site Infrastructure.description:
The Site Infrastructure Service Line is a transversal organization within Air Liquide’s Global Infrastructure and Operations (GIO) responsible for the design, industrialization, and maintenance of the Group's physical and local digital foundations. This includes local area networks (LAN), wide area networks (WAN), Wi-Fi, firewalls, and on-site computing resources across approximately 3,000 sites globally.
The service line is led by Director Olivier Duccini and is structured around global functional teams and regional hubs to ensure technical consistency and operational proximity. Key leadership includes:
Global Teams: The organization focuses on Engineering & Innovation to design infrastructure solutions, and Transition & Operations to manage operational standards and site delivery.
Regional Management: Regional Solution Architects such as Mark Williams (Americas), Erwan Hamon (EAMEI), and Tai Keong Fua (APAC) support local project follow-ups and architectural governance.

Cloud Services.description:
The Cloud Services Service Line is a transversal organization within Air Liquide’s Global Infrastructure and Operations (GIO) responsible for the Group's multi-cloud strategy and environment management. The service line provides a standardized, automated, and secured framework for deploying infrastructure across major providers such as AWS and GCP. Key areas of focus include FinOps for cost optimization, such as the current campaign to delete aged EC2 snapshots to save over $200,000 annually, and the enforcement of security policies like the 1-year maximum lifecycle for Service Account keys.

The service line is also leading several innovation initiatives for the 2027–2030 roadmap:
Cloud Center of Excellence: Establishing a framework built on Platform Engineering and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) to move operations from basic infrastructure toward full-stack management for cloud-native applications.
Sky Bridge: Creating a consistent, secure connectivity fabric and gateway pattern to interconnect on-premise, edge, and multiple cloud providers sovereignly.
Containerization by Default: Making cloud-agnostic containerization the standard build and deploy method to ensure workloads can port freely across providers to leverage the best pricing.
Cloud Brokerage: Enabling single applications to distribute services across several clouds to use the best specific offerings from each CSP.
Wifi on the Cloud: Moving Wi-Fi control planes to the cloud for centralized, AI-assisted operations and faster site rollouts.
Localised Data Backup: Implementing sovereignty-aware backups of critical data to ensure residency and recoverability where specific regulations require it.
